7.3 The contractor shall remove the pipes, poles, planks, clamps after comp letion of works 7.4 Scaffolding measurement is restricted to the actual area of work down s uch as repair of ducts or insulation removal. 7.5 Scaffolding height will be calculated from the level at which it is erected from the resting platform or ground. 8.0 Providing Scaffolding & platform for approach to attend works at 0ML to 15 ML. 8.1 The contractor should bring scaffolding/pipes wooden planks, clamps et c required for the work. 8.2 The contractor should erect the same at the required location/levels and up to a height as directed by NLCIL for rectification of work. 8.3 The contractor shall remove the pipes, poles, planks, clamps after comp letion of works 8.4 Scaffolding measurement is restricted to the actual area of work down s uch as repair of ducts or insulation removal. 8.5 Scaffolding height will be calculated from the level at which it is erected from the resting platform or ground. 9.0 Replacement of damaged diversion plates by bending the 6mm plate as per site condition in Flue gas and Air ducts. 9.1 Damaged diversion plates cut and removed, New plate marked and 'Cut the plate according to required size. 9.2 Move it to bending machine at TS II workshop as instructed /manual jig. 9.3 The plate should be as per actual profile only. Box up. 10.0 Servicing and replacement of Duct supports like Tie rods 10.1 Using chain pulley block duct arms to be loaded. 10.2 Tie rod to be disconnected and taken out new tie rod to be fabricated a nd connected. 10.3 Chain block load to be transferred and to be removed and normalised. 11.0 Fabrication of Duct manhole doors of minimum 508*508mm rectangul ar shape and erection in duct as per NLCIL site engineer instruction. 11.1 Duct manhole door has to be fabricated as instructed by NLCIL enginee r with available angle and channels. 11.2 After fabrication of Door the door has to welded in the duct. 11.3 Gland rope has to fix and all bolt nuts has to be tightened. 12.0 TAPH (Tubular air preheater) duct casing leak attending by welding a t 55 mL 12.1 Erect scaffolding as required. 12.2 Inspect the duct wall for wear. Patch with MS plate as per NLCIL, 12.3 The plate should be as per actual profile only. Box up. 12.4 Welding and Repair has to be done as per NLCIL site engineer instructio n. 13.0 TAPH (Tubular air preheater) duct casing leak attending by proving e xtra supports at 55 ML 13.1 Erect scaffolding as required. 13.2 Inspect the duct wall for welding crack. 13.3 Welding and Repair has to be done as per NLCIL site engineer instructio n 14.0 TAPH (Tubular air preheater) duct casing plates by cutting holes in a MS sheet as per NLCIL site engineer direction at 55 ML 14.1 In Bundle Chamber TAPH, Inlet and Outlet chambers tube area damage d punched sheet holes has to replace with new sheet by cutting holes in 6 mm sheet and has to overlap or has to replace as per NLCIL site in-char

ge direction. 14.2 Necessary welding and Gas cutting has to done in the duct to complete the work. 15.0 TAPH (Tubular air preheater) duct casing leak attending by MS plate at 55 ML 15.1 Damaged duct casing plate has to be removed or by overlapping new p late has to be replace as per NLCIL site in-charge instructions. 15.2 Necessary welding and Gas cutting has to done in the duct to complete the work. 16.0 SA nozzle bend (400 mm ID) fabrication as per site condition. 16.1 As per site conditions Bend angle has to be fabricate 16.2 The bend has to weld in the pipe without any misalignment problems. 17.0 Replacement of SA Nozzle Pipe of 400 mm dia (necessary scaffolding has to erect by contractor for approach, extra charges will not be give n for scaffolding. 17.1 Erect scaffolding as required. 17.2 Cut the worn out pipe and replace the pipe and match the alignment of pipe. 17.3 Removal of scaffolding and Box up. 18.0 Replacement /Repair of Duct bracing pipes(erect the scaffolding for a pproach, cut the damaged bracing pipe and replace new pipe by weldi ng) 18.1 Erect the scaffolding 18.2 Cut the worn out pipe and replace the new pipe or Repair the Bracing pi pe by angle or patch plate. 18.3 One occasion means repair or strengthening one Bracing pipe. 19.0 Sheeting and Lagging removal 19.1 The work includes removal of the sheeting and the lagging in the requir ed areas in order to expose the metallic parts as instructed by the NLCI Lt d officials. The work includes enabling works such as cutting of Lugs, etc. if any, at his own cost. 19.2 The removed reusable insulation materials if any, should be carefully co llected and stacked safely giving protection from wind and rain for re-use. 19.3 Payment will be made based on the measurement of the actual area of lagging removed. 19.4 Sheets should be spread below the area of removal so that the wool is n ot allowed to let fall in the areas below. The loose wool should be packed in gunny sacks for further transportation to designated places as per dire ction of NLCI Ltd officials. 20.0 Providing Lagging 20.1 Lugs or hooks to hold the lagging firmly are to be welded to the metallic part, wherever required. 20.2 Lagging is to be made up to the required thickness as directed by the N LCI Ltd officials. 20.3 The lagging shall be cross-stitched with GI binding wires and tied suitab ly to the lugs or hooks. The joints if any should be staggered. Joints, if any , of Lagging mattresses pieces should be firmly stitched as instructed. 20.4 Materials such as LRB Mattresses, lugs, hooks, etc. will be supplied by NLCI Ltd at free of cost inside TPS-II Expn normally. Sometimes in lieu of LRB Mattress, Cera wool blankets, Insulation/Calcium Silicate and similar blocks may have to be used as per work requirements and as instructed. 20.5 During emergencies, materials required for work such as wool, lugs, etc . are to be brought from PCS/other Units to TPS-II Expn work spot using N

LCIL lorry by the contractor at his own cost. 20.6 All the materials required for the work are to be transported to the work spot from site shed by the contractor at his own cost. 20.7 For welding works, welding machine with a qualified welder to carry out . welding work in the Boiler area should be arranged by the contractor hi mself at his own cost. 20.8 Measurements will be taken only for the finished surfaces of the actual work done after the item work is completed in all respects.1) Immediately after completion of works, the wool insulation, refractory debris /Al / G.I. Sheet / flat / binding wire debris should be collected from various levels ( Heights from "55" ML to "0" ML) of the boilers, packed in sacks and prope rly stacked for measurement at '0 'm level of the respective units in the a rea shown by the NLCIL officials. 20.9 All re-usable materials have to be sorted out and transported to work s hed and accounted as per the directions of NLCIL Officials. 20.10 After taking measurements, the stacked debris has to be transported to the designated areas inside TPS-II Expansion at his own cost. ***** 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses SPECIAL CONDITIONS Part-I 1.0 The contractor should provide all safety appliances, hand lamps and torch lights required for the wo rkmen on his own and the workmen should follow NLCIL safety rules and regulations strictly & scrup ulously. 2.0 Skilled Workers having exclusively adequate experience in lifting and erecting of heavy materials ar e to be engaged independently for ducts. 3.0 Necessary Gate pass approval for men and material shall be obtained well in advance from concern ed department - HOHR/TPS2E/NLCIL. 4.0 The contractor should engage sufficient numbers of workmen and supervisor round the clock till the completion of work .A separate supervisor should be available in all the three shifts to supervise the work 5.0 Readiness of the work front will be intimated one week in advance. 6.0 The Contractor has to strictly adhere to the time frame set by the NLCIL Engineers for each work 7.0 The contractor should engage qualified/certified Electricians in each shift to take care of electrical fi ttings, connections and electrical machines/equipments. 8.0 The contractor should engage independent & separate groups for simultaneously execution of work s in ESP & Ducts. 9.0 The contractor should submit the daily labour report (DLR) in triplicate to the NLCIL shift in-charge i n every shift beginning. 10.0 The following tools and tackles are strictly under the scope of the Contractor and should be availabl e at site as and when required. The quantities mentioned, if any, are just indicative and any addition al requirement should be arranged by the Contractor in short duration. 10.1 Required spanners (ring, double end and box spanners) 10.2 Cutting torch, regulators and keys (minimum 5 sets) 10.3 Gas cutting Hoses for Oxygen and Acetylene - Not less than 200 meters each. 10.4 Welding cable 500 Mtrs. 10.5 Required numbers of Electrode Oven 10.6 Welding Shields, Holders and goggles (each 10 Nos.) 10.7 Sledge hammers - 10 lbs 10.8 Chain pulley blocks of capacity 1T with 5-20m lift, 2T with 5-20m lift, and 5T with 3-7m lift a long with suitable D shackles and wire rope slings - each 5 Nos. 10.9 Canvas slings of various capacity up to 10 T for lifting of materials 10.10 Electrically operated portable rope hoist of 2T capacity with height of lifting 20 - 25m.

10.11 Small and Medium Size Platform trolleys- each 2 Nos. 10.12 Rubber hose for water washing - (50M length - 3/4" size capable of withstanding a water pre ssure of 10 KSC) - 2 Nos. 10.13 Manila rope 1" - 40 Mts. 10.14 Torch lights 10.15 24V transformer with accessories for hand lamps. 10.16 3 phase welding machines (minimum 5 numbers) 10.17 Adequate numbers of Safety belts. 10.18 Safety barricades are to be provided by the contractor in the required areas/ locations. 11.0 Any other tools required for the works are to be provided by the Contractor. The above tools and ta ckles should be checked in with necessary endorsement of Security Officer/TPS-2 Expn. The same en dorsed documents should be handed over to the NLCIL engineers. 12.0 Storing and safeguarding the Tools and tackles are under Contractor’s scope. 13.0 Necessary scaffolding platforms with suitable fixtures are to be arranged by the Contractor, whenev er and wherever required during the execution of works. 14.0 The following materials and consumables will be provided at free of cost by NLCIL. The loss or dam age to the items will be recovered from the contractor's running bill. 14.1 Electricity, compressed air & water. 14.2 M.S. Plates, angles, channels, pipes, I beams required for the works. 15.0 The following materials and consumables will be Scope of contractor. 15.1 Cutting gas (Oxygen and Acetylene (DA)) 15.2 Welding electrodes 15.3 Scaffolding pipes and clamps 15.4 Cotton waste 15.5 Air hoses for cleaning 16.0 Necessary additional and special tools & tackles, if any, may be issued at the discretion of NLCIL en gineers to expedite and complete the works at the earliest and are to be returned to NLCIL immediat ely after completion of work. 17.0 Transport facilities such as Lorry, Cranes, Tractors and etc., will not be provided by NLCIL The Contr actor has to arrange vehicles for material movement and for all other works . 18.0 Operation of critical hydraulic equipments should be carried out under the guidance of NLCIL engine ers. Damages to such critical equipments caused due to mal operation are liable for heavy penalty w ith suitable recovery in running bills. 19.0 The non-availability of front, for the reasons such as equipment stoppage not available and etc., will not be attributed to contractor’s account. 20.0 The food and Canteen facilities are under the scope of the contractor and NLCIL will not extend any facility in this regard. 21.0 The Contractor should arrange additional skilled workforce whenever required, as per the instructio ns of NLCIL Engineers, in a very short period. 22.0 Work place and fabrication area should always be kept neat and easily accessible. The scraps and waste materials collected should be transported and disposed to the designated places after complet ion of works, immediately. 23.0 The Quantum of work will be fixed after inspection of all the ducts. Then site will be handover to con tractor, from handover of site the contractor has to complete all the declared works within work peri od (as per Sl.No.16.2 of Part-II Special Conditions) otherwise PRC will be applicable. Part-II 1.0 SUPERVISOR CHARGES – PENALTY CLAUSE 1.1 In case the specified site supervisor is not engaged by the contractor for the days as per site r equirement, then a penalty of 1.5 times of the supervisory charges shall be deducted fro m the bills of the contractor on pro-rata attendance basis. 1.2 The attendance details of the supervisors shall be maintained with the signature of the super visor, countersigned by the Contractor as well as the NLCIL official concerned. 1.3 Payment of wages to the supervisor and PF and other statutory remittance, if applicable, will b e in the scope of the Contractor. 2.0 Tools & tackles, lifting machines & Safety appliances that are used for the work or by the workmen should posses ISI mark and valid test certificate from the competent authority. 3.0 The Contractor should observe all safety rules and regulations in force and ensure that all necessar y safety precautions are followed up strictly for the safety of workers engaged in the work. 4.0 The Contractor should engage adequate man power having appropriate skills with the approval of t

he NLCIL officials to carryout and complete the works. Any extra time / over time engagement of the man power shall be the contractor’s responsibility. 5.0 RATE OF WAGES The present rates of wages payable to various categories of contract workers and Supervisor are as below: TABLE Wages to be paid Categor Dearness allowanc Total wages y Rate of wages e-(DA) w.e.f (Rs. per day) 01.04.2026 (Rs. per day) (Rs. per day) USK 350.00 206 556 SSK / Su 410.00 240 650 pervisor SK 494.00 287 781 HSK 579.00 339 918 6.0 RATE OF WAGES / DA PAYABLE TO THE WORKMEN The contractor has to pay the rates of wages / DA as per Table above as announ ced by NLCIL and any revision of rates of wages / DA from time to time. Howeve r, in case of any revision of rates of wages / DA notified during contract period, t he contractor shall pay the same along with P.F. & ESI component for the variou s categories of labour component. 7.0 RATE REVISION (NOT APPLICABLE). 8.0 CONTRACT WORKMEN DEATH RELIEF FUND (CWDF) 8.1 An amount equivalent to 0.2% (zero point two percent) of gross value of every bill payable (b efore statutory, non statutory deductions) shall be deducted towards “Contract Workmen Deat h Relief Fund” (CWDF) from the contractors for the works carried out by the contractor. No pro vision has been made in the estimate towards the above deduction. 8.2 Based on the modified DRF scheme, monthly contributions to the death relief fund of Contract Workmen / Supervisors shall be deducted by the Contractor Employers concerned @ Rs.25/- fr om every contract workman / Supervisors engaged by Contractor Employer for the works in NL CIL from their salary /wages payable. In order to facilitate this, necessary deduction will be ma de from the bills of the Contractor employers based on Form - D (Attendance Register) & Form -B (Wage Register) Equal monthly contribution to the fund @ Rs.25/- per contract workman / S upervisors will be made by the Principal Employer NLCIL i.e. the Concerned Unit Head / Unit Ac counts Centre. 9.0 CONTRACT WORKMAN AGE The contractor shall not engage workmen beyond 60 years and the Contractor s hall also produce the required age proof for the workmen engaged by him, while applying for entry permit for first time.

10.0 ESI & EPF The Contractor Employers shall be required to undertake the responsibility of re mitting the contribution/ subscription etc., of the contract workman engaged by them towards EPF (EPF & EDLI), ESI etc., (as applicable) and NLCIL as the princip al employer, will ensure compliance under the relevant applicable statutes by ve rifying the remittance made by the Contractor Employers before releasing part / final bills. 11.0 BONUS The contractor shall ensure payment of minimum bonus of 8.33% of the annual wages to the contract workmen engaged by them for more than 30 days subject to the wages ceiling as provided under Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and failure i n this regard will be treated as violation of the terms of the contract. 12.0 SAFETY Personal protective equipments (PPE)ie like Helmet, Safety shoe, Goggles etc by to be provided by the contractor and it is in the scope of the contractor. 13.0 PRICE REDUCTION CLAUSE Time is the essence of the contract. In case the contractor fails to complete the works within the stip ulated period, then, unless such a failure is due to Force Majeure or due to Purchaser’s defaults (wor k Front Not available), the total contract price shall be reduced by ½% (half percent) of the total con tract price per day of delay or part thereof subject to a maximum of 5% of the total contract price, b y way of reduction in price for delay and not as penalty. 14.0 GUARANTEE FOR WARRANTY Not Applicable 15.0 CONTRACT PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE Not Applicable 16.0 PERIOD OF CONTRACT 16.1 11 months from service start date as per GeM contract. Note: Lead days of 1 day are provided to the Service Provider for necessary mobilization for offering service. Thus the service start date will commence from minimum 1 day after contract genera tion date. 16.2 WORK PERIOD: The work execution period is 60 days from the date of handing over the site. The work has to b e carried out during the Overhaul of Unit-2. 17.0 PAYMENT TERMS 17.1 Part bill will be permitted on monthly basis for the completed work in that month after produci ng required Documents and invoice. 17.2 Final bill will be paid after getting finalization order. Bill will be paid after acceptance of Invoic e within 30 Days. 18.0 GST (Goods and Service Tax) Contractor has to furnish the GST Registration number with relevant docume ntary evidence. Contractor has to comply with the GST Act/ Rules. 19.0 NLCIL reserves the right to short close / extend the contract due to special circumstances.
